items.stem: A quality manager wants to focus improvement on the defects that cause most of the losses. Which tool best identifies them?

options.rationale: Correct: a Pareto chart ranks causes so the vital few driving most loss are visible.
A control chart shows process stability over time, not ranked contribution.
A scatter diagram explores relationships between two variables.
A check sheet collects raw tally data but does not rank or prioritise it.

items.explanation: The Pareto principle focuses effort on the vital few causes.

items.stem: Which step comes first when deploying a strategic plan using a policy-deployment approach?

options.text: Align objectives to the organisation's strategy and define measures
options.rationale: Correct: deployment starts by aligning objectives and measures to strategy.
Supplier audits are an execution activity, not the first deployment step.
Buying equipment is premature before objectives are defined.
Recognition comes after deployment and results.

items.explanation: Strategic deployment begins with alignment of objectives and measures.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate uses of the voice of the customer (VOC)?

options.text: Translating customer needs into measurable product requirements
options.rationale: Correct: VOC turns stated needs into design and process requirements.

options.text: Prioritising improvement efforts by customer impact
options.rationale: Correct: VOC data helps rank what matters most to customers.

options.text: Setting internal defect targets without any customer input
options.rationale: That ignores the customer, defeating the purpose of VOC.
VOC informs quality decisions; it does not replace financial planning.
VOC drives measurement rather than removing it.

items.explanation: VOC is used to define requirements and prioritise by customer impact.
